Q: Application based cms or package for laravel A:

October is pretty much amazing. I think you can do anything with it. When I saw their website the first time on a recommendation of a friend I also saw it as a simple CMS - but look at the documentation- and resources-page: You can create your own plugins, it has a very intricate and easy to understand databse-handling that also manages complicated relationships like "many to many polymorphic" and there is an easy way to create backend-pages that contain forms with those relations. In my opinion its really amazingly thought through and it can serve as CMS-part for almost anything.

Q: Why can't python find some modules when I'm running CGI scripts from the web? A:

I solved this problem by changing user of Apache in Linux Ubuntu by command in terminal:

sudo gedit /etc/apache2/envvars

Please change www-data on export APACHE_RUN_USER and export APACHE_RUN_GROUP to your current user or user that can run python script. Have a good time ;)

Q: What's the C++ equivalent of C#'s decimal type? A:

If you want an exact equivalent then unfortunately you'll need some corresponding implementation of the .NET Decimal type. However since C23 there are new decimal floating-point types including _Decimal128 so you can just use it for most practical purposes, because the set of valid values in .NET System.Decimal is a subset of IEEE 754 decimal128. Be aware that due to the difference in range and precision, sometimes the result will be a bit different even though when both are 128-bit long:

  • .NET Decimal: 96-bit mantissa (~28-29 digits), magnitude ~1028
  • IEEE 754 decimal128: 34-digit mantissa, magnitude ~106144

It's the similar situation to when double in x86 is promoted to 80-bit long double in expressions

In fact GCC, Clang and many other compilers had already supported the IEEE 754 decimal128 type for a long time as an extension before it was added to the C standard. It was available in Sparc and IBM systems for even longer

As an extension, GNU C supports decimal floating types as defined in the N1312 draft of ISO/IEC WDTR24732. Support for decimal floating types in GCC will evolve as the draft technical report changes. Calling conventions for any target might also change. Not all targets support decimal floating types.

The decimal floating types are _Decimal32, _Decimal64, and _Decimal128. They use a radix of ten, unlike the floating types float, double, and long double whose radix is not specified by the C standard but is usually two.

6.14 Decimal Floating Types

That means you don't need to newest C version to use. It's also usually available as an extension in C++, or you can use the std::decimal proposal here. You can also see a similar type in Rust
